q: Do the paper's extrapolated NOT/CNOT/Toffoli/T-depth counts for full-scale SIMON32/64 through SIMON128/256 (Tables 4-5) actually match a byte-accurate reversible synthesis, or are they optimistic estimates that omit ancilla-management overhead?
basis: This replication only exercised the 20-qubit reduced instance (n=3, T=4). The paper's full-scale resource tables cover ~thousand-qubit oracles that we did not build. Independent audits of Grover-oracle resource counts for other lightweight ciphers (e.g. Grassl et al. AES) have historically differed by 10-30% from initial paper estimates once uncomputation, comparator chaining, and T-parallelization are done rigorously.
next_steps: Rebuild SIMON32/64 reversible oracle end-to-end in Qiskit or Q# using the paper's Section 3.3 spec at full width; run Qiskit `count_ops()` and a T-depth pass (e.g. pyLIQTR or a manual T-parallel scheduler); compare gate-by-gate against the paper's Table 4 numbers for SIMON32/64 first (smallest full variant). Free execution on uicgpu or CherryRd CPU; no quantum hardware needed --- resource counting is pure circuit analysis.

q: Does the Grover-on-SIMON attack extend cleanly to other lightweight block ciphers with similar Feistel-like structure (SPECK, PRESENT, GIFT, LED), and if so, what is the T-depth ratio Grover-SIMON : Grover-SPECK for equal key length?
basis: SIMON's round function uses only AND, XOR, and rotation --- unusually Toffoli-cheap. SPECK adds modular addition (multi-qubit ripple-carry adder), PRESENT uses an S-box (Toffoli-heavy). Naive expectation: SPECK Grover oracle should have 2-4x more Toffolis per round than SIMON at matched key length. The paper does not compare across ciphers.
next_steps: Port the reduced-instance oracle template to SPECK32/64 and PRESENT-80 (both have published reversible circuits in the literature: Jaques et al. 2020 for SPECK, Almazrooie et al. for PRESENT). Reuse this replication's Grover harness (diffuser + phase kickback + iteration schedule are cipher-agnostic). Compare per-round Toffoli counts and total T-depth for equal (n, k, T). Free: standard Qiskit.

q: How robust is the Grover-on-SIMON success probability under realistic noise models (depolarizing, T1/T2, gate infidelity), and at what error-per-gate threshold does the peak-on-K signal drop below the second-best key by less than 2 sigma?
basis: The paper's simulation is noise-free statevector. Real Grover circuits are notoriously fragile because the amplification is coherent --- any dephasing broadens the histogram and mixes marked/unmarked amplitudes. Recent work (Cai, Xu 2022) has shown Grover circuits with >30 sequential Toffolis lose >50% of amplification at p_error ~ 1e-3 per two-qubit gate. Our 4-iteration reduced SIMON oracle has ~200 Toffolis --- squarely in that regime.
next_steps: Rerun `code/grover_simon.py` with Qiskit-Aer noise model: sweep depolarizing p in {1e-4, 1e-3, 5e-3, 1e-2} and record the K-vs-K' peak ratio and combined marked-key probability. Add a T1/T2 model calibrated to IBM Eagle / IonQ Aria published numbers. Plot degradation curve; identify break-even threshold. Free: Qiskit-Aer + AerSimulator(method='density_matrix').

q: What is the concrete resource cost of Grover-on-SIMON128/256 under a specific surface-code overhead (d = 15, 21, 27), and how does it compare to the NIST post-quantum security-level-5 threshold?
basis: The paper reports T-count and T-depth but leaves surface-code magic-state distillation and routing overhead as future work. NIST PQC categorizes security level 5 as 'approximately as hard as key search on AES-256' --- a threshold that Craig Gidney's 2020 AES-256-under-Grover estimate placed at ~10^13 T-gates and ~7000 logical qubits. SIMON128/256 has been argued (informally) to be comparable, but no rigorous FT cost estimate exists.
next_steps: Feed the paper's Table 5 T-count/T-depth for SIMON128/256 into Litinski's magic-state factory calculator (or Beverland et al.'s Azure Quantum Resource Estimator, which is free and web-based). Report logical qubits, physical qubits at p=1e-3, and total runtime for one Grover iteration at d=15,21,27. Cross-reference against Gidney's AES-256 numbers; write up whether SIMON128/256 hits NIST PQC level 5 with the same surface-code parameters. Free: Azure QRE + arXiv Litinski calculator.

q: Does the paper's oracle construction interact with quantum side-channel attacks (e.g. amplitude-amplification-assisted key-recovery under partial known-plaintext, or coset-based algebraic attacks combined with Grover) in ways that offer better-than-quadratic speedup for SIMON-like ciphers?
basis: SIMON's linear layer is bit-rotation-only --- it commutes with certain algebraic symmetries that Simon's algorithm (unrelated to the cipher name) can exploit for period-finding. Kaplan et al. (2016) showed that some lightweight ciphers admit Q2-model attacks with exponential speedup when Simon's algorithm is chained with Grover. The paper avoids this direction --- worth checking whether the reversible oracle we built here could be repurposed.
next_steps: Read Kaplan et al. 2016 'Breaking Symmetric Cryptosystems Using Quantum Period Finding' and Bonnetain-Naya-Plasencia 2019. Check whether SIMON's round function under a fixed key admits a nontrivial period on the plaintext; if so, prototype a Simon-on-SIMON circuit reusing this replication's reversible encrypt_inplace block. Compare query complexity to Grover-only. Free: analytical work + small Qiskit sim; no hardware.
